name: Pecheneg
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Extinct Turkic; Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description is Menges 1944-45 wordlist-or-less; no grammar covering stress

sources.citation: Jazyki mira: Tjurkskie jazyki (1997), Prilozhenie: Tipovye skhemy statej, pp. 537-538 (template IV for short articles on individual/dead languages).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Defines 5.1.0 as 'Фонологические сведения (включая сведения об ударении, тоне и т.д.)' -- used to confirm that Shcherbak's article had a slot for stress and left it empty.
Nothing on phonology or stress; cites Multitree, Dietrich, Wenzel 1860, Howorth 1880, Paroń 2021.

sources.citation: Paroń, Aleksander. 2021. The Pechenegs: Nomads in the Political and Cultural Landscape of Medieval Europe (East Central and Eastern Europe in the Middle Ages 450-1450, 74). Leiden: Brill. Open access.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (historical monograph). p.19 n.80 gives the bibliography 'On the language of the Pechenegs': Németh 1921-25, 1930, 1932, 1971; Menges 1944-45; Shcherbak 1959; Vörös 2002. a full-text search for stress/accent/phonolog finds no linguistic statement.

sources.citation: Shcherbak, A. M. 1997. Pechenezhskij jazyk. In: Tenishev, E. R. (ed.), Jazyki mira: Tjurkskie jazyki, 107-110. Moskva: Indrik.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. 5.1.0 'Фонологические сведения' (p.109) gives only a 'hypothetically established' vowel/consonant inventory and five sound changes (g/gh > j > 0, spirantization k > x, labialization a > o, etc.); 5.1.1 syllable types; 5.1.2 (alternations) 'Данных нет'. The series template IV (p.538) explicitly assigns stress/tone to 5.1.0, so the silence is the author's. p.108: material = proper names, toponyms, ethnonyms only; 'нет ни одного печенежского текста'.

sources.citation: Dietrich, Ayse. n.d. 'The Pechenegs – Script.' Humanities Institute teaching note, 2 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; states knowledge of the language 'comes from proper names, toponyms, ethnonyms and a few artifacts'.
